title: btmesh: Fix for crash in UAT CBs
description: Fixing crashes in UAT callbacks. Closes #17460.

notes.body: Should not compute_ascii_key() ensure to always initialize the pointer instead?

Probably the best solution would be to change to something similar as in "packet-pdcp-lte.c".
The binary keys values are there defined using pattern:
```
   guint8   rrcCipherBinaryKey[16];
   gboolean rrcCipherKeyOK;
```
I am not not sure why here the binary values are dynamically allocated since in this context the size of the keys are always constant.

As of compute_ascii_key(), this function is complicated. On the other hand it is used in the same context. I can think of moving g_free() into the function for better control of inputs. Then, use `*ascii_key = NULL;` for all exit cases.
At first glance the function is not that complicated and the only thing missing is setting *key = NULL in line 4594 (this is already done in places were the function returns -1).
I have found another, less critical problem an I will try to amend the Merge request...
Then it is as easy as initializing ascii_key to NULL at the beginning of the function, which is more elegant than your current proposal.

Why not check whether `rec->network_key_length` is -1, instead, as that's what `compute_ascii_key()` returns on an error?

That avoids the need to set `*err` to NULL on success, which you currently aren't doing.

This applies to all the *other* checks of `*err` as well.

Also, is the error string being freed in all cases where it's returned?  (Presumably the reason why you added the error strings is so that they can be reported to the user in the future; I'm not seeing any code that currently returns them.)

This is code is base on other UAT CB. They assume `*err` is NULL on entry (uat_load.l, line 309), and freed by the caller (see comment in uat.h starting from line 108, and uat_load.l line 322).

As of `*err == NULL`, this the most universal way of checking if an error occurred. Only the first error should be reported (one error string allocated) to avoid error string leak (only the last one is freed).

I would stay with the code as it is now, unless you still got strong opinion on it.

Fixing white space only.

> As of `*err == NULL`, this the most universal way of checking if an error occurred.

"Universal" in the sense of "universal in UAT code", presumably; it's hardly anywhere near universal in all of Wireshark, much less in all code out there.
This could probably use some API review, but that appears to be a UAT-wide issue, so we'll go with this for now.
